input.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: Nova Scotia is not on our accepted list, but it is Sparkling's own home jurisdiction (Dartmouth, NS) rather than Garman's (Saskatchewan), the venue is non-exclusive and there is no arbitration seated abroad — so the clause favours us and is not walk-away territory. We note the off-list law rather than redlining it.

input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) (reinforced by Section 3(c)) is a blanket consent requirement with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, which is walk-away territory for us. We proposed a free assignment right to affiliates and successors, a reasonableness standard for other assignments, and confirmation that a change of control gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right.
